items.en: a big instrument with black and white keys
items.example: She's learning to play the piano.

items.en: an instrument that you hit with sticks
items.example: He plays the drums.

items.en: a person who acts in films or plays
items.example: Who is your favourite actor?

items.en: the people who watch or listen to a show
items.example: The audience loved the show.

items.en: a building where people go to watch plays
items.example: We went to the theatre last night.

items.en: a story that actors perform in a theatre
items.example: We saw a play by Shakespeare.

items.en: a set of TV programmes about the same people or subject
items.example: I'm watching a new crime series.

items.en: a show on TV or radio (US: program)
items.example: What's your favourite TV programme?

items.en: a TV station
items.example: What's on the other channel?

items.en: a funny film or play
items.example: I prefer comedies to horror films.

items.en: a long story in a book
items.example: I'm reading a novel by Jane Austen.

items.en: a person who writes books
items.example: Who is the author of this book?

items.en: a description of events that can be true or invented
items.example: My grandmother tells great stories.

items.en: a thin book with pictures and articles that comes out every week or month
items.example: I bought a magazine for the train.

items.en: printed pages with the news that come out every day
items.example: My father reads the newspaper every morning.

items.en: the last part of a story or a film
items.example: The film has a happy ending.

items.en: making you laugh
items.example: The film was really funny.

items.en: not interesting
items.example: The book was so boring.

items.en: making you feel happy and interested
items.example: The last part of the film is really exciting.

items.en: to watch or listen to something on the internet without downloading it
items.example: We streamed a film last night.

items.en: the kind of person someone is
items.example: She has a warm personality.

items.en: the qualities that make a person different or a person in a story
items.example: He has a strong character.

items.en: kind and nice to other people
items.example: Everyone at the school is very friendly.

items.en: caring about other people and wanting to help them
items.example: It was very kind of you to help me.

items.en: always telling the truth
items.example: Be honest. Do you like my haircut?

items.en: able to wait calmly without getting angry
items.example: Teachers need to be very patient.

items.en: not wanting to work or do anything
items.example: My cat is very lazy.

items.en: working with a lot of effort
items.example: She's a hard-working student.

items.en: nervous about talking to people you do not know
items.example: He was very shy as a child.

items.en: quick at learning and understanding things
items.example: She's a very clever girl.

items.en: not clever
items.example: That was a stupid mistake.

items.en: happy to give money or time to other people
items.example: My uncle is very generous.

items.en: thinking only about yourself
items.example: Don't be so selfish! Share your sweets.

items.en: happy and smiling a lot
items.example: She is always cheerful in the morning.

items.en: quiet and not often laughing or joking
items.example: He looks serious but he's very funny.

items.en: that you can trust to do what they say
items.example: We need a reliable person for this job.

items.en: thinking about what you do so that you do not make mistakes
items.example: Be careful with that knife!

items.en: not thinking enough about what you do
items.example: It was a careless mistake.

items.en: not afraid of danger
items.example: The firefighters were very brave.

items.en: thinking carefully and making good decisions
items.example: That's a sensible idea.

items.en: calm and not worried
items.example: My dad is very relaxed about everything.

items.en: making people follow rules
items.example: Our teacher is strict but fair.

items.en: treating everyone in the same right way
items.example: That's not fair!

items.en: how you feel at a certain time
items.example: You're in a good mood today!

items.en: to act in a certain way
items.example: The children behaved very well today.

items.en: what you think about something
items.example: In my opinion the film was too long.

items.en: to have the same opinion as someone
items.example: I agree with you.

items.en: to have a different opinion from someone
items.example: I'm sorry but I disagree with you.

items.en: to like one thing more than another
items.example: I prefer tea to coffee.

items.en: happy because you or someone close to you did something good
items.example: We're very proud of our daughter.

items.en: unhappy because someone has something that you want
items.example: He's jealous of his brother's new bike.

items.en: feeling shy or silly in front of other people
items.example: I was so embarrassed when I fell over.

items.en: sad and worried because something bad happened
items.example: She was upset about her exam results.

items.en: thinking a lot about a problem and feeling unhappy
items.example: I'm worried about my mum.

items.en: happy about something
items.example: I'm pleased with my new flat.

items.en: afraid
items.example: I'm scared of spiders.

items.en: a little angry
items.example: I was annoyed because the bus was late again.

items.en: not able to understand something
items.example: I'm confused. Can you explain it again?

items.en: happy because something bad did not happen
items.example: I was relieved when I found my keys.

items.en: the feeling that you have when you are afraid
items.example: She has a fear of flying.

items.en: the feeling of being angry
items.example: He couldn't hide his anger.

items.en: the feeling of being happy
items.example: Money doesn't always bring happiness.

items.en: a thought or a plan
items.example: That's a great idea!

items.en: a way of thinking about something
items.example: I understand your point of view.

items.en: to look like something or to give the feeling of being something
items.example: You seem tired today.

items.en: knowing that something is true
items.example: Are you sure?

items.en: very likely
items.example: It will probably rain tomorrow.

items.en: possibly
items.example: Maybe we can meet next week.

items.en: to feel annoyed or worried about something
items.example: Do you mind if I open the window?

items.en: very bad
items.example: The weather was terrible.

items.en: the air and water and land around us
items.example: We must protect the environment.

items.en: to use something again or make it into something new
items.example: We recycle all our glass and paper.

items.en: collecting old things so that they can be used again
items.example: Put the bottles in the recycling.

items.en: things that you throw away because you do not need them
items.example: We produce too much waste.

items.en: a light material that is used to make bags and bottles and many other things
items.example: Try not to use so much plastic.

items.en: a metal container for food (US: can)
items.example: Put the empty tins in the yellow bin.

items.en: dirty air or water or land
items.example: Air pollution is a big problem in cities.

items.en: the usual weather in a place
items.example: The climate here is warm and dry.

items.en: changes in the weather of the world because it is getting warmer
items.example: Climate change is a serious problem.

items.en: power from electricity or gas or the sun that makes machines work
items.example: Solar panels make energy from the sun.

items.en: a flat thing on a roof that makes electricity from the sun
items.example: We put solar panels on our roof.

items.en: to stop a light or a machine by pressing a button
items.example: Switch off the lights when you leave.

items.en: to put something in the bin because you do not want it
items.example: Don't throw away that box.

items.en: to use something again
items.example: You can reuse these bags.

items.en: to make something smaller or less
items.example: We want to reduce our waste.

items.en: a very large round thing in space such as the Earth
items.example: We only have one planet.

items.en: animals and plants that live in nature
items.example: The park is full of wildlife.

items.en: grown without chemicals
items.example: I try to buy organic vegetables.

items.en: old plants and food that become good soil for the garden
items.example: We put our vegetable waste on the compost.

items.en: a large container in the street where you put empty bottles
items.example: Take the empty bottles to the bottle bank.

items.en: rubbish that people leave in the street
items.example: There's a lot of litter in the park.

items.en: not bad for the environment
items.example: Cycling is an eco-friendly way to travel.

items.en: working with power from a plug or a battery
items.example: She drives an electric car.

items.en: the feeling of being hot or very hot weather
items.example: I can't sleep in this heat.

items.en: a lot of water that covers land that is usually dry
items.example: The flood destroyed many homes.

items.en: to get information about something
items.example: Can you find out what time the train leaves?

items.en: to stop doing something
items.example: I gave up smoking last year.

items.en: to find information in a book or on the internet
items.example: Look up the word in a dictionary.

items.en: to make a machine quieter or less strong
items.example: Please turn down the music.

items.en: to make a machine louder or stronger
items.example: Can you turn up the heating?

items.en: to put something back in its usual place
items.example: Put your toys away, please.

items.en: to enter a room or a building
items.example: Come in and sit down.

items.en: to return to a place
items.example: I want to go back to Italy next year.

items.en: to start a journey
items.example: We set off early in the morning.

items.en: to have no more of something
items.example: We've run out of milk.

items.en: to feel happy about something that will happen
items.example: I'm looking forward to the holidays.

items.en: to become an adult
items.example: I grew up in a small village.

items.en: to move something to a later time
items.example: Don't put off your homework until Sunday.

items.en: to continue doing something
items.example: Carry on. I'm listening.

items.en: to go less fast
items.example: Slow down! You're driving too fast.

items.en: to do something more quickly
items.example: Hurry up or we'll be late!

items.en: to write something on paper so that you do not forget it
items.example: Write down my phone number.

items.en: to stop working because of a problem
items.example: Our car broke down on the motorway.

items.en: to visit someone at their home
items.example: Come round for coffee tomorrow.

items.en: to eat in a restaurant
items.example: We usually eat out on Fridays.

items.en: to return home or to a place
items.example: What time did you get back last night?

items.en: to become less angry or nervous
items.example: Calm down. It's only a game.

items.en: to become happier or to make someone happier
items.example: Cheer up! Tomorrow will be better.

items.en: to do exercise to get fit or to find the answer to something
items.example: I work out at the gym twice a week.

items.en: to deal with a problem or to put things in order
items.example: Don't worry. I'll sort it out.

items.en: a polite way to ask someone for help
items.note: "Could" is more polite than "can". Use it with people you do not know.

items.en: a very polite way to ask someone to do something
items.note: After "mind" use the -ing form: Would you mind closing the door?

items.en: a polite way to say what you want to do
items.note: I'd = I would. Use it in shops and offices and on the phone: I'd like to pay by card.

items.en: a polite way to ask for something in a shop or café
items.note: "Could I have the bill, please?" sounds much friendlier than "Give me the bill."

items.en: an informal way to ask if you can do something
items.note: Good with friends and colleagues: Is it OK if I leave a bit early today?

items.en: a polite way to ask if you can do something
items.note: Answer "No, not at all." if it is OK. Here "no" means yes!

items.en: a way to suggest doing something together
items.note: Use the verb without "to": Let's go to the cinema.

items.en: a friendly way to make a suggestion
items.note: "Why don't we meet at six?" is a suggestion and not a real question.

items.en: a way to suggest something
items.note: Use a noun or the -ing form: How about a coffee? How about going for a walk?

items.en: a way to suggest something or to offer to do something
items.note: Mostly used in questions with "I" and "we": Shall we take a taxi? Shall I help you?

items.en: a way to say yes to a suggestion
items.note: Shorter: Good idea! or Sounds good!

items.en: a polite way to say no to an invitation or a request
items.note: "I'm afraid" makes a no softer. It does not mean that you are scared.

items.en: a friendly way to say no now but yes later
items.note: Say it after you say no to an invitation: Sorry, I'm busy tonight. Maybe another time.

items.en: a way to ask if someone has time on a certain day
items.note: Are you free on Thursday evening? Answer: Yes, I am. or No, sorry. I'm busy.

items.en: a polite way to ask which time is good for someone
items.note: Here "suit" means "be good for". You can also ask: When is good for you?

items.lemma: I'd like to make an appointment.
items.en: what you say when you want to book a time with a doctor or an office
items.note: We "make" an appointment. Not: do an appointment.

items.en: a way to ask for a different time
items.note: You can also say: Can we move the appointment to Friday?

items.lemma: I need to cancel my appointment.
items.en: what you say when you cannot come at the time you booked
items.note: Call as early as you can. Some places charge a fee if you cancel late.

items.en: a friendly way to say goodbye when you will meet again on a certain day
items.note: See you on Monday! Without a day: See you soon!

items.en: what you say when you arrive late
items.note: Give a short reason: Sorry I'm late. The bus was delayed.

items.lemma: Could you say that again, please?
items.en: a polite way to ask someone to repeat something
items.note: Shorter: Sorry? or Pardon? with your voice going up at the end.

items.lemma: Could you speak more slowly, please?
items.en: a polite way to ask someone to talk more slowly
items.note: Very useful on the phone. Most people are happy to help.

items.en: a way to ask someone to explain what they said
items.note: Say it in a friendly voice. With a hard voice it can sound rude.

items.en: a way to thank someone for helping you
items.note: Also: Thanks a lot! or Thank you so much!

items.en: a friendly answer when someone thanks you or says sorry
items.note: Also: You're welcome. or Don't worry about it.
